problems.stem: What distinguishes structural color from pigment-based color?
options: Structural color is produced by geometry interacting with light rather than chemical dyes alone
Structural color is always painted on after manufacturing
Structural color works only in darkness
Structural color eliminates all wavelength dependence
problems.explanation: Structural color emerges from how micro- and nano-scale architecture manipulates light.

problems.stem: Why is the Morpho butterfly a classic biomimetic optics example?
options: Its color comes mainly from thick surface paint
Its wing architecture creates strong optical effects through layered microstructure
Its color is unrelated to surface structure
problems.explanation: Morpho coloration is widely studied because geometric structure, not only pigment, creates the visible effect.

problems.stem: Which engineering application best fits structural-color principles?
options: Anti-counterfeit surfaces that change appearance through microstructure
A steel beam designed only for compressive load
A hydraulic seal selected only for friction
A battery chosen only for energy density
problems.explanation: Structural-color principles are especially useful for optical sensing, signaling, and anti-counterfeit design.

problems.stem: What should a designer control first when engineering a structural-color surface?
options: The geometric spacing and arrangement of the optical microstructure
Only the total mass of the part
The electrical voltage of the package
problems.explanation: Optical behavior depends strongly on structural scale and spacing relative to wavelengths of light.
